entities.summary: Abu Sa'id Aban ibn Taghlib ibn Rabah al-Kindi, known as al-Jarīrī, was a Shia Muslim jurist, muhaddith, qāriʾ, mufassir, and disciple of Shia Imams Ali al-Sajjad, Muhammad al-Baqir, and Ja'far al-Sadiq. Born in the 8th century, he flourished during the Umayyad Caliphate and contributed to the development of Shia legal theology. Al-Jarīrī's works had a lasting impact on Shia thought and jurisprudence, shaping the intellectual landscape of the Islamic world. His teachings on hadith (narrations of the Prophet Muhammad's sayings and actions) and jurisprudence influenced many Shia scholars and communities. Al-Jarīrī's legacy can be seen in the continued study and practice of Shia legal theology, which remains an essential component of Shia identity and practice to this day. The impact of al-Jarīrī's work on Shia thought and jurisprudence is evident in the many Shia scholars and communities that have followed in his footsteps, and his teachings continue to be studied and debated by scholars and theologians around the world.

entities.summary:
Abu Sa'id Aban ibn Taghlib ibn Rabah al-Kindi, known as al-Jarīrī, was a prominent Shia Muslim jurist, muhaddith, qāriʾ, mufassir, and disciple of Shia Imams Ali al-Sajjad (680–712), Muhammad al-Baqir (712–732), and Ja'far al-Sadiq (732–765).









Al-Jarīrī's contributions significantly impacted Shia Islamic jurisprudence, and his works were passed down through generations, influencing Islamic scholarship and jurisprudence. His teachings on hadith and qāriʾ played a crucial role in shaping Shia Islamic theology and practice.




Al-Jarīrī's significance extends beyond his scholarly contributions; his work as a muhaddith helped establish hadith as a vital component of Shia Islamic scholarship.









The study of al-Jarīrī's life and works continues to be an essential aspect of Shia Islamic studies, providing valuable insights into the development of Shia theology and jurisprudence.
